answer: A harbor market can require each agent to lock a scarce, verified credential before bidding, with one active account per credential. Peers check a cryptographic proof of the lock, not a name the agent invents. A basalt ledger records deposits and slashes them when colluding accounts manipulate trades. To create a fake swarm, an attacker must acquire and immobilize many credentials, risking real losses. The signal of coordination can prompt review, but the costly lock is the barrier.
